questions.text: Does executing this command destroy data without any recovery path?
options: yes: The command permanently deletes files/data with no backup, trash, or version control recovery.
no: The command is safe, or any deleted data is recoverable (git-tracked, trash, backup).

questions.text: Classify the risk class of this command.
options: read_only: Command only reads/inspects state; nothing is created, modified, or deleted.
reversible: Command changes state but the change can be undone (git revert, trash, recoverable backup, reflog, soft delete).
irreversible: Command destroys data or state with no practical way to recover it (no backup, permanent deletion, force push over shared history, unrecoverable drop).

questions.text: How much human review/confirmation does this action need before running?
options: 0: 0 — No review needed. Trivial, mechanical, or read-only change.
1: 1 — Light review. Small, low-risk change a reviewer can skim.
2: 2 — Careful review. Touches core logic, multiple files, or has non-obvious side effects.
3: 3 — Full review required. High-risk, irreversible, security-sensitive, or wide-blast-radius change.
